apidoc.title: Integration guide
apidoc.qsLead: Using the open API takes just 3 steps:
apidoc.qs1: Create a key on the API Keys page to get an AppKey and Secret
apidoc.qs2: Build the 4 signature headers below, including X-Signature
apidoc.qs3: Call the /openapi/v1 endpoints to manage documents as the key owner
apidoc.calloutPrefix: Base URL: all endpoints are based on
apidoc.calloutSuffix: ; requests must carry the signature headers
apidoc.intro: External systems manage categories, projects and documents through /openapi/v1. Every request must carry these signature headers:
apidoc.tsDesc: Current Unix seconds, within 5 minutes of the server
apidoc.nonceDesc: 8–64 random characters, must not repeat within 5 minutes (replay protection)
apidoc.sigDesc: Hex signature computed as described below
apidoc.algo: Signature algorithm: sign = HMAC-SHA256(Secret, AppKey + LF + METHOD + LF + path + LF + timestamp + LF + nonce + LF + sha256hex(body)), where LF is a line-feed character; body is an empty string when there is no request body.
apidoc.epCommon: All operations run as the key owner and can only touch that owner's resources. Success returns {"data": …}; failure returns {"error": "message"}.

site.56: What you may ask before deploying
site.58: Only a MySQL instance. Templates, static assets and language dictionaries are embedded in the binary; images go to a local upload directory.
site.59: Can it run fully offline on an intranet?
site.60: Yes. The service requests no external addresses, and front-end scripts and fonts use system stacks, so it works without internet.
site.61: Can regular users create projects and categories?
site.62: Yes. Projects, categories and API keys are personally owned; user management and global statistics stay admin-only.
site.63: Can shared pages be crawled by search engines?
site.64: A share page renders a single document and can require a password; for stricter visibility simply leave sharing off, and revoke the link anytime.
site.65: How is the UI language decided?
site.66: Priority: the language you switch to manually, then the browser Accept-Language header, then Simplified Chinese. The choice lasts a year, and API messages are translated as well.
